entities.name: Chronic myeloid leukemia
entities.anchor: CML → BCR::ABL1.
rearr: Defining — BCR::ABL1, usually t(9;22)
entities.pitfall: ABL1 kinase-domain resistance mutations are acquired evolution events, not the initiating CML lesion.

entities.name: Polycythemia vera
entities.anchor: PV → JAK2.
snv: Driver — JAK2 V617F or exon 12 activating indels
other: Cooperating — copy-neutral 9p loss of heterozygosity can increase mutant JAK2 dosage
entities.pitfall: CALR and MPL are characteristic of ET/PMF rather than conventional PV.

entities.name: Essential thrombocythemia
entities.anchor: ET → JAK2, CALR or MPL.
snv: Alternative drivers — JAK2 V617F; CALR exon 9 frameshift; MPL activating variants
entities.pitfall: Triple-negative cases exist; genotype does not distinguish ET from prefibrotic PMF.

entities.name: Primary myelofibrosis
entities.anchor: PMF shares the JAK2–CALR–MPL triad.
snv: Alternative drivers — JAK2 V617F; CALR exon 9 frameshift; MPL activation
Cooperating — ASXL1, SRSF2, EZH2, IDH1/2, U2AF1
entities.pitfall: Prefibrotic and overt fibrotic phases are combined. Additional lesions influence progression rather than define PMF alone.

entities.name: Chronic neutrophilic leukemia
entities.anchor: CNL → CSF3R T618I.
snv: Driver — CSF3R membrane-proximal activating variants, especially T618I
Cooperating — SETBP1, ASXL1
entities.pitfall: A CSF3R mutation is interpreted with the neutrophilic phenotype and exclusion of mimics.

entities.name: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia
entities.anchor: CEL: clonal eosinophilia without a defining kinase fusion.
snv: Recurrent, nonspecific — ASXL1, TET2, SRSF2, STAT5B (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Exclude PDGFRA/B, FGFR1, JAK2 and other defining kinase-fusion neoplasms before using this category.

entities.name: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia
entities.anchor: JMML → RAS pathway.
snv: Drivers — PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS; NF1 or CBL inactivation
other: Predisposition — NF1/CBL may be germline with a somatic second hit; not all RASopathy-associated myeloproliferation is JMML
entities.pitfall: Interpret the molecular profile with morphology and lineage; no single listed lesion is sufficient in isolation.

entities.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, NOS
entities.anchor: An MPN phenotype can remain unclassifiable.
snv: Driver — JAK2, CALR or MPL in subsets
entities.pitfall: No unique NOS mutation; this is an exclusion category, not a fourth driver-defined MPN.

entities.name: Systemic mastocytosis
entities.anchor: Systemic mast cells → KIT, usually D816V.
snv: Driver — KIT D816V; other activating KIT variants in subsets
Cooperating — SRSF2, ASXL1, RUNX1, TET2 in advanced disease
entities.pitfall: Includes mast cell leukemia. Indolent and advanced systemic forms share KIT biology; KIT does not establish aggressiveness.

entities.name: Mast cell sarcoma
entities.anchor: Mast cell sarcoma does not reliably carry KIT D816V.
snv: Reported — activating KIT variants in a subset
entities.pitfall: Very rare; no universal recurrent molecular driver is established. Do not extrapolate the usual systemic-mastocytosis genotype.

entities.name: Myelodysplastic neoplasm
entities.anchor: MDS: splicing, epigenetics, del(5q), or multi-hit TP53.
snv: Subset-defining — SF3B1; biallelic TP53 inactivation
Drivers/cooperating — TET2, ASXL1, SRSF2, U2AF1, ZRSR2, RUNX1, STAG2
cnv: Associated — −7/del(7q), del(20q), +8; complex changes in TP53-altered cases
entities.pitfall: Morphologic, low-blast and increased-blast forms combined. Adult clonal hematopoiesis mutations alone do not diagnose MDS.

entities.name: Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia
entities.anchor: CMML → TET2 + SRSF2; add RAS for proliferation.
snv: Recurrent — TET2, SRSF2, ASXL1
Cooperating/proliferative — NRAS, KRAS, CBL, PTPN11
entities.pitfall: The TET2/SRSF2 combination is a useful association, not specific enough to replace persistent monocytosis and morphology.

entities.name: MDS/MPN with neutrophilia
entities.anchor: Dysplastic neutrophilia → SETBP1, ASXL1, ETNK1.
snv: Recurrent — SETBP1, ASXL1, ETNK1; RAS-pathway variants
entities.pitfall: Formerly atypical CML. BCR::ABL1 is absent; distinguish from CSF3R-driven CNL.

entities.name: MDS/MPN with SF3B1 mutation and thrombocytosis
entities.anchor: SF3B1 dysplasia + JAK2 proliferation.
snv: Defining — SF3B1 in the named genetic category
Cooperating — JAK2 V617F; less often CALR or MPL
entities.pitfall: A morphologic ring-sideroblast/thrombocytosis category can be used in SF3B1-wildtype cases under specified WHO criteria.

entities.name: MDS/MPN, NOS
entities.anchor: Overlap phenotype; no unique driver.
snv: Recurrent — ASXL1, TET2, SRSF2, RAS-pathway alterations (variable)
entities.pitfall: No mutation combination substitutes for excluding defined MDS/MPN, MDS and MPN entities.

entities.name: Acute myeloid leukemia
entities.anchor: AML: transcription-factor fusions or NPM1/CEBPA, with cooperating signaling lesions.
snv: Subset-defining — NPM1; CEBPA
Cooperating — FLT3 ITD/TKD, KIT, NRAS/KRAS, IDH1/2, DNMT3A
Myelodysplasia-related — ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1, ZRSR2
cnv: Associated — −5/del(5q), −7/del(7q), complex karyotype; TP53 loss in subsets
rearr: Subset-defining — RUNX1::RUNX1T1; CBFB::MYH11; KMT2A, MECOM or NUP98 rearrangements
Subset-defining — DEK::NUP214, RBM15::MRTFA; rare BCR::ABL1
Rare molecular subsets — CBFA2T3::GLIS2 and other recurrent fusions
entities.pitfall: Broad AML entry combines genetic and differentiation categories; APL is separate for its exceptionally strong fusion association. FLT3 ITD is an insertion/duplication, not a fusion.

entities.name: Acute promyelocytic leukemia
entities.anchor: APL → PML::RARA.
rearr: Defining — PML::RARA t(15;17)
entities.pitfall: Other RARA-family fusions can produce an APL-like phenotype but are biologically distinct; this cue refers to PML::RARA-positive APL.

entities.name: Myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome
entities.anchor: Trisomy 21 + GATA1s, then additional hits.
snv: Driver — GATA1 truncation producing GATA1s
Cooperating — cohesin, epigenetic and signaling-gene alterations
entities.pitfall: Transient abnormal myelopoiesis shares GATA1 and is excluded as a separate malignancy here.

entities.name: Myeloid sarcoma
entities.anchor: AML genetics outside the marrow.
snv: Subset drivers — NPM1, FLT3, RAS-pathway or other AML-associated variants
rearr: Subset drivers — RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11, KMT2A and other AML fusions
entities.pitfall: No sarcoma-specific driver; evaluate with the underlying myeloid disease.

entities.name: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with tyrosine kinase fusion
entities.anchor: Eosinophilia can point to a kinase fusion.
rearr: Defining subsets — FIP1L1::PDGFRA; ETV6::PDGFRB; ZMYM2::FGFR1; PCM1::JAK2
Other defining families — FLT3 fusions, ETV6::ABL1 and other recognized kinase fusions
entities.pitfall: Examples are not the only partners. Eosinophilia can be absent; a cryptic deletion can generate FIP1L1::PDGFRA.

entities.name: Acute leukemia of ambiguous lineage
entities.anchor: Mixed lineage can share ALL/AML fusion biology.
snv: Cooperating — FLT3, RAS-pathway and epigenetic-gene variants (variable)
rearr: Defining subsets — BCR::ABL1; KMT2A rearrangement; ZNF384 rearrangement
Subset — BCL11B rearrangement/activation
entities.pitfall: Includes mixed-phenotype and acute undifferentiated leukemia. Lineage assignment still requires immunophenotypic criteria.

entities.name: B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma
entities.anchor: B-ALL: fusions and chromosome dosage define many subsets.
snv: Subset-defining — PAX5 P80R; IKZF1 N159Y
Cooperating — RAS, JAK-pathway alterations; PAX5 loss-of-function
cnv: Defining subsets — high hyperdiploidy; hypodiploidy; iAMP21
rearr: Subset-defining — BCR::ABL1, ETV6::RUNX1, TCF3::PBX1; KMT2A rearrangements
Other subsets — DUX4, ZNF384, MEF2D, NUTM1, PAX5 rearrangements; TCF3::HLF
Ph-like subsets — ABL-class fusions; CRLF2 or JAK2 rearrangements
entities.pitfall: A broad umbrella: these are alternative molecular groups, not a combined expected profile.

entities.name: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma
entities.anchor: CLL: del(13q), trisomy 12, and heterogeneous signaling/splicing lesions.
snv: Recurrent — NOTCH1, SF3B1, TP53, ATM, BIRC3
entities.pitfall: IGHV mutation status reflects B-cell maturation history; it is not an oncogenic driver mutation. BTK/PLCG2 resistance lesions are not baseline defining events.

entities.name: Hairy cell leukemia
entities.anchor: Classic hairy cell → BRAF V600E.
snv: Driver — BRAF V600E in the great majority
entities.pitfall: BRAF-wildtype cases require careful distinction from other splenic B-cell neoplasms; no single mutation is absolutely tumor-specific.

entities.name: Splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukemia with prominent nucleoli
entities.anchor: Former HCL variant: think MAP2K1, not classic BRAF.
snv: Driver — MAP2K1 (subset)
Cooperating — TP53 (subset)
entities.pitfall: WHO5 includes former hairy-cell leukemia variant and some former B-prolymphocytic leukemias.

entities.name: Splenic diffuse red pulp small B-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Red pulp lymphoma: CCND3 and BCOR associations.
snv: Recurrent — CCND3, BCOR (subsets)
entities.pitfall: No unique molecular hallmark; the splenic architecture and phenotype matter.

entities.name: Marginal zone lymphoma
entities.anchor: MALT fusions converge on NF-κB; splenic cases often involve NOTCH2/KLF2.
snv: Drivers — NOTCH2, KLF2 (splenic-enriched); TNFAIP3, KMT2D and other NF-κB/chromatin lesions (site-dependent)
cnv: Associated — del(7q) in splenic MZL; trisomies 3/18 in subsets
rearr: MALT subsets — BIRC3::MALT1; IGH::MALT1; BCL10::IGH; IGH::FOXP1
other: Context — chronic antigenic stimulation, infection or autoimmunity in selected anatomical settings
entities.pitfall: Splenic, nodal and extranodal/MALT forms combined with site-specific molecular notes. Do not apply a gastric MALT fusion frequency to all MZL.

entities.name: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma
entities.anchor: LPL/Waldenström → MYD88 L265P.
snv: Driver — MYD88 L265P
Cooperating — CXCR4 truncating variants (subset)
entities.pitfall: MYD88 is neither universal nor specific to LPL; it also occurs in selected large B-cell lymphomas.

entities.name: Follicular lymphoma
entities.anchor: Follicular → IGH::BCL2 plus chromatin modifiers.
snv: Drivers/cooperating — KMT2D, CREBBP, EZH2
rearr: Characteristic — IGH::BCL2 t(14;18), especially classic FL
entities.pitfall: BCL2 rearrangement can be absent, especially in specific variants. Duodenal-type disease is included here.

entities.name: Pediatric-type follicular lymphoma
entities.anchor: Pediatric-type FL often lacks BCL2 rearrangement.
snv: Recurrent — MAP2K1, TNFRSF14, IRF8
entities.pitfall: Pediatric-type refers to biology, not an absolute age cutoff; this differs from conventional adult-type FL.

entities.name: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
entities.anchor: A skin follicle-center lymphoma often lacks the classic FL translocation.
snv: Recurrent — TNFRSF14 and chromatin-regulator alterations (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Strong BCL2 expression or rearrangement prompts consideration of systemic FL involving skin; exceptions occur.

entities.name: Mantle cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Mantle → CCND1 beside an immunoglobulin enhancer.
snv: Cooperating — ATM, TP53, NOTCH1/2
rearr: Characteristic — IGH::CCND1 t(11;14)
Alternative — CCND2 or CCND3 rearrangement in cyclin-D1-negative cases
entities.pitfall: The rearrangement drives cyclin expression, not a conventional chimeric kinase. Leukemic non-nodal disease is included.

entities.name: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
aliases: T cell histiocyte rich large B cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: DLBCL has multiple BCR/NF-κB and chromatin routes.
snv: Subset drivers — MYD88, CD79B, CARD11; EZH2, CREBBP, KMT2D; NOTCH2, TNFAIP3
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B loss; BCL2 gains in subsets
rearr: Subset alterations — BCL6, BCL2 or MYC rearrangements
entities.pitfall: Includes NOS and T-cell/histiocyte-rich morphology. MYC plus BCL2 rearrangements define a distinct category; double protein expression is not double-hit genetics.

entities.name: Large B-cell lymphoma of immune-privileged sites
entities.anchor: CNS/testis/eye LBCL → MYD88–CD79B and immune escape.
snv: Recurrent — MYD88 L265P, CD79B; PIM1
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B loss; 9p24.1 gains in subsets
entities.pitfall: CNS, vitreoretinal and testicular disease share enriched pathways, not a universal mutation.

entities.name: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type
entities.anchor: Leg-type LBCL often uses MYD88/CD79B.
snv: Recurrent — MYD88 L265P, CD79B
entities.pitfall: The name is a clinicopathologic entity; lesions can arise outside the leg.

entities.name: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Intravascular LBCL: BCR/NF-κB alterations in a distinctive growth pattern.
snv: Recurrent — MYD88, CD79B (subsets)
entities.pitfall: Intravascular growth defines the phenotype; the genotype overlaps other LBCLs.

entities.name: Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Mediastinal B-cell → JAK/STAT and 9p24.1.
snv: Recurrent — STAT6, SOCS1, TNFAIP3
rearr: Recurrent — CIITA rearrangements (subset)
entities.pitfall: Mediastinal location alone is insufficient; integrated phenotype distinguishes it from other LBCLs.

entities.name: Mediastinal gray zone lymphoma
entities.anchor: Gray zone shares PMBCL/Hodgkin immune-escape biology.
snv: Recurrent — SOCS1, STAT6 (subsets)
entities.pitfall: An integrated mediastinal diagnosis; there is no unique diagnostic driver.

entities.name: DLBCL / high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements
entities.anchor: Double hit means two rearrangements: MYC + BCL2.
rearr: Defining — MYC rearrangement together with BCL2 rearrangement; BCL6 can additionally be rearranged
entities.pitfall: MYC/BCL6-only cases do not belong to this WHO5 MYC/BCL2 category.

entities.name: High-grade B-cell lymphoma, NOS
entities.anchor: High-grade morphology can lack a defining genetic category.
snv: Heterogeneous — TP53 and other aggressive B-cell lymphoma lesions
rearr: Subset — isolated MYC rearrangement
entities.pitfall: An exclusion category; not equivalent to Burkitt lymphoma or MYC/BCL2 double-hit disease.

entities.name: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration
entities.anchor: Burkitt-like appearance, characteristic 11q gain/loss.
cnv: Defining — proximal 11q gain with distal 11q loss
entities.pitfall: Typically lacks a MYC rearrangement; the dosage pattern is more informative than one gene.

entities.name: Large B-cell lymphoma with IRF4 rearrangement
entities.anchor: IRF4-rearranged LBCL is a separate molecular entity.
rearr: Defining — IRF4 rearrangement, commonly with an immunoglobulin locus
entities.pitfall: MUM1/IRF4 protein staining alone does not establish rearrangement.

entities.name: ALK-positive large B-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: ALK in a B-cell lymphoma, often CLTC::ALK.
rearr: Defining — ALK fusion; CLTC::ALK is common
entities.pitfall: Distinguish from ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma using lineage.

entities.name: EBV-associated large B-cell lymphomas
aliases: fibrin associated large B cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: For EBV-associated LBCL, the virus may be the strongest molecular cue.
snv: Variable cooperating — TP53, TNFAIP3 and other immune/signaling lesions
entities.pitfall: Study umbrella for EBV-positive DLBCL, chronic-inflammation-associated LBCL, fibrin-associated LBCL and lymphomatoid granulomatosis; these remain distinct clinicopathologic diagnoses.

entities.name: Plasmablastic lymphoma
entities.anchor: Plasmablastic lymphoma: MYC often joins EBV.
rearr: Frequent cooperating — MYC rearrangement
other: Viral — EBV in a substantial subset
entities.pitfall: Plasma-cell markers alone do not distinguish this lymphoma from plasma cell myeloma.

entities.name: Primary effusion lymphoma
entities.anchor: PEL → KSHV/HHV8.
other: Defining viral association — KSHV/HHV8; EBV co-infection common
entities.pitfall: Includes extracavitary PEL. No universal recurrent human SNV or fusion defines the disease.

entities.name: KSHV/HHV8-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: HHV8-positive LBCL is distinct from PEL.
entities.pitfall: Often occurs in the context of HHV8-associated multicentric Castleman disease; morphology and phenotype distinguish it from PEL.

entities.name: Fluid overload-associated large B-cell lymphoma
aliases: HHV8 unrelated effusion large B cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: An effusion lymphoma can be HHV8-negative.
entities.pitfall: No established single defining genetic driver. HHV8 negativity and clinical/effusion context help distinguish it from PEL.

entities.name: Burkitt lymphoma
entities.anchor: Burkitt → MYC–immunoglobulin rearrangement.
snv: Cooperating — ID3, TCF3, CCND3
rearr: Characteristic — IGH::MYC; IGK/IGL–MYC alternatives
other: Viral — EBV association varies by biological group
entities.pitfall: MYC rearrangement is not specific for Burkitt; high-grade B-cell differentials require integrated evaluation.

entities.name: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma
entities.anchor: Hodgkin: JAK/STAT, NF-κB and immune escape.
snv: Recurrent — SOCS1, STAT6, TNFAIP3
entities.pitfall: Histologic subtypes combined; many tumor mutations are hard to detect in bulk tissue because tumor cells are sparse.

entities.name: Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma
entities.anchor: LP-cell disease remains distinct from classic Hodgkin.
snv: Recurrent — SGK1, DUSP2, JUNB (subsets)
rearr: Recurrent — BCL6 rearrangements (subset)
entities.pitfall: WHO5 retains this name; other classification systems use nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma.

entities.name: Plasma cell myeloma
entities.anchor: Myeloma: hyperdiploidy or IGH translocation, then progression hits.
snv: Drivers/cooperating — KRAS, NRAS, BRAF; TP53 in progression
rearr: Subsets — IGH::CCND1; IGH::NSD2/FGFR3 (t(4;14)); IGH::MAF; IGH::MAFB
Progression — MYC rearrangements
entities.pitfall: Includes plasma cell leukemia as a presentation. NSD2 and FGFR3 dysregulation can arise from the same t(4;14) event.

entities.name: Plasmacytoma
entities.anchor: A localized plasma-cell tumor can share myeloma alterations.
cnv: Recurrent — aneuploidy and plasma-cell-neoplasm copy-number changes
rearr: Subset — IGH rearrangements involving cyclin-D genes or other myeloma-associated partners
entities.pitfall: Solitary bone and extraosseous plasmacytomas combined. A myeloma-like alteration does not itself establish systemic myeloma.

entities.name: Heavy chain diseases
entities.anchor: Abnormal truncated immunoglobulin heavy chain is the clue.
snv: Functional lesion — IGH deletions/sequence changes producing a truncated heavy chain
entities.pitfall: Alpha, gamma and mu forms combined; this is not a single oncogenic fusion category. Specific recurrent initiating cancer drivers remain incompletely characterized.

entities.name: T-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma
entities.anchor: T-ALL → NOTCH1 plus T-cell transcription programs.
snv: Driver — NOTCH1 activation; FBXW7 loss
Cooperating — PTEN, IL7R, JAK1/3, RAS-pathway lesions
rearr: Subset drivers — TAL1/STIL::TAL1, TLX1, TLX3, LMO1/2, HOXA or BCL11B activation
entities.pitfall: Includes early T-precursor disease; its signaling/epigenetic profile differs from conventional T-ALL.

entities.name: T-cell prolymphocytic leukemia
entities.anchor: T-PLL → TCL1A/MTCP1 activation plus ATM loss.
snv: Cooperating — ATM; JAK1, JAK3, STAT5B
rearr: Characteristic — TCR-locus rearrangements activating TCL1A, or MTCP1
entities.pitfall: TCL1 activation and defective DNA-damage response are complementary molecular themes.

entities.name: T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia
entities.anchor: T-LGL → STAT3; selected cases STAT5B.
snv: Driver — STAT3 SH2-domain variants; STAT5B in selected subsets
entities.pitfall: TCR clonality is not itself an oncogenic rearrangement and can also occur in nonmalignant expansions.

entities.name: NK-large granular lymphocytic leukemia
entities.anchor: Chronic NK expansion can involve STAT3.
snv: Driver — STAT3 (subset)
entities.pitfall: Formerly chronic lymphoproliferative disorder of NK cells. Distinguish from aggressive NK-cell leukemia.

entities.name: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma
entities.anchor: ATLL → HTLV-1 plus TCR/NF-κB signaling.
snv: Cooperating — PLCG1, PRKCB, CARD11, VAV1, CCR4
rearr: Subset — CTLA4::CD28 or ICOS::CD28
other: Etiologic — HTLV-1 integration and viral oncogenic programs
entities.pitfall: Acute, lymphoma, chronic and smoldering presentations combined.

entities.name: Mycosis fungoides
entities.anchor: MF: heterogeneous T-cell signaling and tumor-suppressor loss.
snv: Recurrent — PLCG1, STAT3/5B, TP53 and other TCR/JAK-STAT lesions
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B, TP53 loss (especially advanced disease)
entities.pitfall: No universal driver; TCR clonality supports a clone, not malignancy by itself.

entities.name: Sézary syndrome
entities.anchor: Sézary → T-cell signaling plus ZEB1/cell-cycle loss.
snv: Recurrent — PLCG1, CARD11, CCR4, TP53
entities.pitfall: Separate leukemic cutaneous T-cell entity; not simply a genetic subtype of MF.

entities.name: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma, systemic
aliases: ALK positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma
ALK negative anaplastic large cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: ALCL: ALK fusion, or ALK-negative JAK/STAT alternatives.
snv: ALK-negative subsets — JAK1, STAT3 activation
rearr: ALK-positive defining — NPM1::ALK and alternative ALK partners
ALK-negative subsets — DUSP22 or TP63 rearrangements
entities.pitfall: ALK-positive and ALK-negative molecular groups are retained inside this broad entry; DUSP22 and TP63 are not equivalent biologically.

entities.name: Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Implant-associated ALCL → JAK/STAT; usually ALK-negative.
snv: Recurrent — JAK1, STAT3 (subsets)
entities.pitfall: The implant-associated clinical setting defines this entity; do not equate it with systemic ALK-positive ALCL.

entities.name: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Skin ALCL: DUSP22 rearrangement in a subset.
rearr: Subset — DUSP22 rearrangement
entities.pitfall: Most cases lack ALK rearrangement. Distinguish from systemic ALCL involving skin and lymphomatoid papulosis.

entities.name: Nodal T-follicular helper cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: TFH lymphoma → RHOA G17V + TET2/DNMT3A.
snv: Drivers/cooperating — RHOA G17V, TET2, DNMT3A
Enriched subset — IDH2 R172 in angioimmunoblastic-type disease
rearr: Subset — ITK::SYK, especially follicular-type
entities.pitfall: Angioimmunoblastic, follicular and NOS forms combined. TET2/DNMT3A may arise in antecedent clonal hematopoiesis.

entities.name: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS
entities.anchor: PTCL-NOS has no single defining mutation.
snv: Variable drivers/cooperating — TET2, DNMT3A, VAV1, PLCG1, TP53
entities.pitfall: Exclude TFH, ALCL, viral and other defined T-cell entities before using NOS.

entities.name: Hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Hepatosplenic → i(7q), STAT5B and SETD2.
snv: Recurrent — STAT5B, STAT3, SETD2
entities.pitfall: Includes alpha-beta and gamma-delta lineages; no alteration is universal.

entities.name: Enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Celiac-associated intestinal lymphoma → JAK/STAT.
snv: Recurrent — JAK1, STAT3 and epigenetic-regulator variants
cnv: Associated — 9q gains and other complex changes
entities.pitfall: Do not merge the biology with MEITL, which is usually not celiac-associated.

entities.name: Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: MEITL → SETD2 + STAT5B/JAK3.
snv: Recurrent — SETD2 inactivation; STAT5B, JAK3 activation
entities.pitfall: Formerly EATL type II; the obsolete type-II label does not imply celiac disease.

entities.name: Intestinal T-cell lymphoma, NOS
entities.anchor: Intestinal T-cell malignancy without a defining category.
entities.pitfall: No established single molecular hallmark; exclude EATL, MEITL and secondary intestinal involvement.

entities.name: Indolent T-cell lymphoma of the gastrointestinal tract
aliases: indolent T cell lymphoproliferative disorder GI
entities.anchor: Indolent GI T-cell lymphoma can have JAK/STAT lesions.
snv: Subset — STAT3 and other JAK/STAT pathway alterations
rearr: Subset — STAT3::JAK2
entities.pitfall: WHO5 uses lymphoma terminology; do not confuse with indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder.

entities.name: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma: no universal somatic driver.
other: Predisposition — germline HAVCR2 variants in a subset, especially with immune dysregulation
entities.pitfall: HAVCR2 is a susceptibility association, not a tumor-specific somatic finding. Alpha-beta lineage differs from cutaneous gamma-delta lymphoma.

entities.name: Primary cutaneous gamma-delta T-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Cutaneous gamma-delta lymphoma → JAK/STAT in subsets.
snv: Driver — STAT3 or STAT5B activation (subset)
entities.pitfall: Separate from panniculitis-like alpha-beta lymphoma despite possible subcutaneous involvement.

entities.name: Primary cutaneous aggressive epidermotropic CD8-positive T-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Aggressive CD8 epidermotropism; no universal driver.
snv: Subset — JAK/STAT pathway alterations
entities.pitfall: Exclude indolent acral CD8-positive lymphoproliferative disorder, which is outside the malignant-only scope.

entities.name: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Extranodal NK/T → EBV + JAK/STAT.
snv: Cooperating — STAT3, JAK3, DDX3X, TP53 (subsets)
entities.pitfall: The old nasal-type name does not limit disease to the nose.

entities.name: Aggressive NK-cell leukemia
entities.anchor: Aggressive NK leukemia often combines EBV with signaling lesions.
snv: Recurrent — JAK/STAT-pathway variants; TP53, DDX3X in subsets
entities.pitfall: EBV-negative cases occur; the fulminant clinical/lineage picture distinguishes it from NK-LGL leukemia.

entities.name: EBV-positive nodal T- and NK-cell lymphoma
entities.anchor: Nodal EBV-positive T/NK disease is a distinct category.
entities.pitfall: No universal SNV/CNV/fusion hallmark is established for memorization. Exclude secondary nodal involvement by extranodal NK/T lymphoma.

entities.name: Systemic EBV-positive T-cell lymphoma of childhood
entities.anchor: Childhood systemic T-cell lymphoma → clonal EBV-positive T cells.
entities.pitfall: Not equivalent to infectious mononucleosis, hemophagocytic syndrome alone or all chronic active EBV disease.

entities.name: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm
entities.anchor: BPDCN: epigenetic lesions; MYC/MYB rearrangements in subsets.
snv: Recurrent — TET2, ASXL1, ZRSR2 and other epigenetic/splicing lesions
cnv: Cooperating — CDKN2A/B, RB1 and other recurrent losses
rearr: Subset — MYC enhancer hijacking, including RUNX2 regulatory regions; MYB rearrangements
entities.pitfall: No single alteration is obligatory; plasmacytoid dendritic lineage is essential.

entities.name: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
entities.anchor: LCH → MAPK activation.
snv: Driver — BRAF V600E; MAP2K1 and other MAPK variants
rearr: Rare — BRAF and other kinase fusions
entities.pitfall: A clonal myeloid neoplasm with a wide clinical spectrum; mutation does not predict extent by itself.

entities.name: Erdheim–Chester disease
entities.anchor: ECD → BRAF/MAPK.
snv: Driver — BRAF V600E, MAP2K1, KRAS/NRAS, ARAF (alternative subsets)
entities.pitfall: Included as a systemic histiocytic neoplasm; behavior is heterogeneous and is not inferred from BRAF alone.

entities.name: Histiocytic sarcoma
entities.anchor: Histiocytic sarcoma can converge on MAPK.
snv: Driver — BRAF, MAP2K1, KRAS/NRAS (subsets)
Cooperating — CDKN2A, TP53 alterations
entities.pitfall: Some cases are clonally related to a prior lymphoid neoplasm; genetic overlap does not replace lineage assessment.

entities.name: Langerhans cell sarcoma
entities.anchor: Malignant Langerhans morphology; no uniform driver.
snv: Reported — MAPK-pathway alterations in a subset
entities.pitfall: Do not presume the mutation distribution of LCH applies to this much rarer sarcoma.

entities.name: Interdigitating dendritic cell sarcoma
entities.anchor: A rare dendritic sarcoma with limited molecular evidence.
snv: Reported — BRAF/MAPK alterations in rare cases
entities.pitfall: No well-established recurrent defining alteration; phenotype and exclusion of mimics remain central.

entities.name: Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma
aliases: inflammatory EBV positive follicular dendritic cell sarcoma
entities.anchor: FDC sarcoma: NF-κB dysregulation; EBV in the inflammatory variant.
snv: Recurrent — NFKBIA, CYLD and other NF-κB-regulator lesions (subsets)
other: Viral — EBV in inflammatory EBV-positive follicular dendritic cell sarcoma
entities.pitfall: Stromal/mesenchymal lineage despite its traditional placement with dendritic tumors; conventional and inflammatory EBV-positive forms are noted together.

entities.name: Fibroblastic reticular cell tumor, malignant
entities.anchor: Reticular-cell malignancy has no established molecular signature.
entities.pitfall: Extremely rare; no validated recurrent driver is available for a reliable memorization cue.

coverage.basis: WHO-HAEM5 nomenclature, with broad study families and selected molecular distinctions retained. WHO authors’ 2022 classification papers are the baseline; the public draft structure can contain older terminology.
merged: AML differentiation and genetic subsets combined except APL; MDS subtypes combined.
B-ALL and T-ALL molecular subsets nested inside broad lineage entries.
Marginal zone lymphomas and selected EBV-associated LBCL categories combined, with aliases and internal distinctions.
Post-cytotoxic, germline-predisposition and immune-dysregulation settings are qualifiers on underlying disease, not separate repeated mutation lists.
Histologic Hodgkin, follicular, ALCL and TFH variants grouped where suitable.
excluded: CHIP/CCUS, MGUS, monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis, in situ lymphoid lesions and transient abnormal myelopoiesis are not separate malignant entries.
Reactive histiocytoses, Castleman disease, lymphomatoid papulosis and indolent cutaneous lymphoproliferative disorders excluded.
Uncertain/provisional NK-lymphoblastic categories and nonmalignant mature plasmacytoid proliferations are not independently catalogued.
limitations: Broad-family coverage is not a certified exhaustive WHO code crosswalk.
Rare lymphomas have limited driver evidence; several entries deliberately emphasize virus or lack of a defining alteration.
LCH and ECD are included as clonal histiocytic neoplasms; clinical aggressiveness varies widely.
Somatic mutations shared with clonal hematopoiesis do not establish a malignancy without diagnostic context.
